Saudi Arabian Oil Co Reports Higher Quarterly Earnings on Stronger Demand

Saudi Arabian Oil Co reported a rise in quarterly earnings on Thursday, attributing the results to robust global demand and higher average crude oil prices. The world’s largest oil exporter said net profit for the three months ended March 31 increased to 129.8 billion riyals ($34.6 billion), up from 117.5 billion riyals a year earlier.

Revenues climbed 8% to 393.2 billion riyals, supported by an uptick in international energy consumption and stable production volumes. The company’s CEO, Amin Al-Nasser, said in a statement, “Saudi Arabian Oil Co continues to deliver strong financial and operational performance in a dynamic market. Our disciplined approach allows us to support energy security while investing in future growth.”

The company’s average daily crude production for the quarter was 10.3 million barrels, in line with its commitments to OPEC+ agreements. Capital expenditure rose 12% year-on-year as the company proceeds with expansion projects in both upstream and downstream segments.

Analysts welcomed the results as a sign of resilience. “These figures reflect the ongoing recovery in oil markets and Saudi Arabian Oil Co’s ability to maintain efficiency,” said Nourah Al-Rashid, an energy analyst at Gulf Resource Partners.

The company reaffirmed its commitment to shareholder returns, announcing a quarterly dividend of $19.5 billion, unchanged from previous quarters.

Industry observers note that Saudi Arabia’s energy sector continues to benefit from steady demand in Asia and improving market stability. The Saudi Energy Ministry stated that its long-term investment plan remains on track, with a continued focus on sustainability and technological innovation.
